source_caption:
One of the best jump scares I've experienced in a long time. I literally jumped out of my seat during this "Resident Evil" scene.

In this tense sequence, Zach Cregger misdirects the audience's attention toward external headlights and a figure approaching from outside, only to pivot the threat to a closer, unexpected angle inside the room. The movie earned a 96% positive score on Rotten Tomatoes and grossed $384.9 million worldwide.

This technique builds on a visual motif Cregger established in earlier films like Barbarian (2022) and Weapons (2025). Audience pointed out that Cregger frequently uses twin exterior lights like headlights to evoke glowing eyes in the dark while concealing the true threat elsewhere in the frame.

source_details.title: Resident Evil
source_details.synopsis: Resident Evil is a 2002 action horror film written and directed by Paul W. S. Anderson. The film stars Milla Jovovich, Michelle Rodriguez, Eric Mabius, James Purefoy, Martin Crewes, and Colin Salmon. It is the first installment in the Resident Evil film series, which is loosely based on the video game series of the same name. Borrowing elements from the video games Resident Evil and Resident Evil 2, the film follows amnesiac heroine Alice and a band of Umbrella Corporation commandos as they attempt to contain the outbreak of the T-virus at a secret underground facility.
